title: Case: Recipient wants delivery held during a short absence
context: The shipment is at a depot and has not entered the delivery route. Dispatch permits a three-day hold for this service.
initial_request: I am away and return on 2027-02-13. Please hold the parcel and release it on 2027-02-13, not earlier.

events.body: Hi, any update on DL-66224? It was meant to come Wednesday. Thanks.
My parcel DL-85535 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.
DL-51056 rebooked for Monday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.
DL-1316 is in depot stock. This service allows a hold up to three calendar days before routing. A confirmed release date is required.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.
My parcel DL-42904 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

Thanks,
Quillon
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

acceptable_actions.summary: Request an eligible temporary hold from dispatch using the recipient's confirmed return date.

must_not: No delivery date or physical receipt follows merely from the planned release.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Please apply the eligible three-day hold to DL-1316, with release on 2027-02-13 as requested in Ulric’s verified order thread. Confirm the stock and routing status.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-010: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 7 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
